Water & Drainage 
  
Drainage and Flood Alleviation 
Engineering and Environmental Consultants were appointed in December 2019 for Flood 
Risk Management works on the Deansgrange Stream. This is a 4-to-5-year project. 
Activities completed to date include additional survey work, CCTV surveys, a Constraints 
Study, Hydrological analysis, and hydraulic modelling. Optioneering, environmental 
surveys and engagement with key stakeholders continue. A Ground Investigation 
Contract is complete. We have received preliminary approval from Irish Rail to tunnel 
under the rail line. Public Consultation on the preferred option took place on the 13th 
December. The environmental impacts review is almost completed.  The Part 8 
submission is proposed shortly. 
  
Engineering and Environmental Consultants have also been appointed for Flood Risk 
Management Works on the Carrickmines/Shanganagh Rivers. This is a 5+ year project. 
Data gathering is underway. A Flow/Rainfall Survey is complete. Further topographical 
survey work has been done. Early damage/benefits assessments are underway to ensure 
a cost-beneficial scheme is achievable. An initial public engagement is complete following 
short briefing sessions with Area Councillors. The Hydrology/Hydraulic report is now 
complete.  The on-site Site Investigation work is largely completed. The options for the 
project are being considered. Interim technical reports have been developed for some 
option locations due to the complexity. 
  
The Monkstown environs flood risk mapping project is substantially completed, and final 
draft mapping and draft options have been submitted for review.

Tourism Development 
 
Cruise Welcome, training, artwork & staff 
The 1st four cruise ships arrived this month into Dun Laoghaire harbour. Upon arrival the 
guests are greeted with large scale welcome imagery of the area. On their way out of 
the harbour they then see visuals suggesting places to see in the county. 
 
Staff training took place for the panel of welcome staff to welcome the guests over the 
summer. The staff were briefed on what guests can see, do and the wealth of events 
available to the guests throughout the year. 
 
A new welcome kiosk was branded and placed in the harbour. The new kiosk was 
wrapped in dlr colours and shows icons of the local landmarks. 
 
Piloting Walking Tours  
With the arrival of the 1st cruise ships there is a pilot walking tour programme in place to 
guide guests around the town and into the bars/restaurants.  
 
Zipit – Zip Trail Opening 
On 24th April Zipit launched their new 30-minute additional zip lining course to their 
Tibradden facility. The investment of €200,000 by Cool Running Events was launched by 
Minister Catherine Martin and attended by representatives from dlr Tourism, Coillte & 
Failte Ireland. 
 
Quarterly Ezine  
Our 1st quarterly ezine went out at the start of the month with all the reopened activities 
this spring along with upcoming events. 
 
Coastival 2023 
DLR Tourism are collaborating on the development of a new summer festival in Dun 
Laoghaire called Coastival. Preparations & planning of events during the new Coastival 
Festival are ongoing.

 Dún Laoghaire Harbour 
  
Cruise Ship Business 
The Cruise Ship Season has commenced with approximately 95 Cruise Ships booked in 
for 2023 at present with over 160,000 passengers and 68,000 crew. We are working 
with the Tourism Department, the Dun Laoghaire Business Association and the Dun 
Laoghaire Chamber of Commerce to maximise the local benefits of the cruise visitors. 
  
Grant Funding 
The Brexit Adjustment Local Authority Marine Infrastructure (BALAMI) Scheme 2022 – 
2023 from the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine has launched a Second 
Tranche call for applications. Dún Laoghaire Harbour received over €3 million in grant 
funding from the first tranche. We submitted 5 grant applications to this scheme by the 
deadline of 30th September 2022 and have been awarded another €1 million in grant 
funding for improvements on the Carlisle Pier.  
  
Projects: 
  
National Watersports Campus 
DLRCC in partnership with Irish Sailing and the Irish Underwater Council have been 
approved in principle for Stream 1 Grant funding for the development of a National 
Watersports Campus. We have responded to requests for additional information and are 
now finalising the grant process and agreements with the project partners.  An MOU has 
been signed with Irish Sailing and Diving Ireland in order to set out and agree the 
objectives of the project. 
  
A concept brochure was presented to the Elected Members during the February 2023 
Council meeting and has since been published. It is hoped that this initiative will assist in 
building momentum and support for the project.  
  
Berth 2 Fenders (Carlisle Pier) 
A project to replace the Berth 2 Fenders has been given approval to proceed to 
procurement stage. RPS Group have been appointed to carry out the design and 
procurement for this project. This project was tendered, and Sorensen Construction have 
been appointed to deliver the project. We are awaiting Foreshore Consent to proceed to 
works on site.

14 | P a g e 
 
 
Grant funding has recently been secured for the installation phase of this project from 
the recent Brexit Local Authority Marine Infrastructure Scheme.  
  
Berth 3 Fenders (Carlisle Pier) 
Grant funding has recently been secured for a project to replace the Berth 3 Fenders 
from the recent Brexit Local Authority Marine Infrastructure Scheme. The project has 
been given approval to proceed to procurement stage. RPS Group have been appointed 
to carry out the design and procurement for this project as it is a mirror image of the 
Berth 2 Fender project.  
  
Carlisle Pier Deck repairs and lighting 
Grant funding has recently been secured for a project to resurface the deck of the 
Carlisle Pier and install lighting towers from the recent Brexit Local Authority Marine 
Infrastructure Scheme. The contactor is now on site and works are progressing well. This 
project should be completed by late May 2023. 
  
East Pier Revetment Repairs 
Grant funding has recently been secured for a project to repair the sloping revetment at 
the back (east side) of the East Pier from the recent Brexit Local Authority Marine 
Infrastructure Scheme. This revertant provides the primary protection for the East Pier 
and has suffered some damage over recent years from the larger storms. Punch 
Consulting Engineers have been appointed to design and manage the project which is 
likely to be on site during the summer of 2023. Cunningham Civil & Marine have been 
appointed to carry out the works on this project and it is due to commence on site in 
June/July this year.   
  
Ferry Terminal 
Retrofit works have commenced in the front office portion of the ferry terminal building, 
and this section is nearing completion. The tenant hopes to have the first sub-tenants on 
site in Q2 2023. 
  
Dublin Array Windfarm 
The developers of the Dublin Array Windfarm have approached the Harbour about the 
possibility of establishing an Operations and Maintenance Base for the windfarm. It is 
hoped that there might be synergies with the Ferry Terminal project. Early engagement 
is ongoing with the developer’s team to establish the exact requirements.  
  
Coastival Festival 2023 
The Biennial Dun Laoghaire Regatta is due to take place in July 2023. We are working 
with several DLRCC departments to expand this into a week-long festival named 
“Coastival” for the Dun Laoghaire Town and Harbour areas. This is planned to run from 
1st – 9th July and many DLRCC departments are involved in putting together a schedule 
of events.

Municipal Services 
 
The Ballyogan Regional Temporary Rest Centre opened its doors to Ukrainian nationals 
on 28 April. The Rest Centre continues to accommodate up to 300 displaced Ukrainian 
nationals for short periods. Over 3,000 people have stayed at the Centre for short 
periods.  
   
As part of a comprehensive wrap around service, accommodation services at the Centre 
are being supported by HSE staff including Environmental Health, Public Health and 
COVID-19 services. The HSE is providing onsite support to meet the healthcare needs of 
Ukrainian residents, and residents also have access to an offsite GP service 7 days a 
week.   
   
Among the facilities available in the temporary rest Centre is separate laundry and 
sanitary facilities, internet access, television spaces, games consoles, games room, 
chessboards, use of bikes and scooters, libraries of Ukrainian books for children and 
adults, translation services, as well as online access to Ukrainian newspapers and 
magazines.   
   
Additionally, orientation and information sessions, basic English language lessons and an 
arts and music entertainment programme is being developed both onsite and nearby 
offsite.
